chapter: Setting the record straight on Hendersonia
title: Correcting Hendersonia on his late 1928 Columbus band personnel
summary: Checking a discography, Horace supplies trombonists Nathaniel Atkins and Ed Fant, tenor Joe Thomas, drummer Jimmy King, banjoist Luke Stewart and trumpeter Jonah Jones for his 1928 band.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: I would like, since we have a little more time, and a little more tape here, in going over, especially some of the material from the book and Hendersononia. There are some quotes in here that were basically in the area where, the pages that were dealing more with you, and, first of all, there -- you might be able to clear up some things concerning questions of personnel in various bands at various times, and I'll just read a graph to you here.

It says, "There are other reports that Horace left his band this summer of 1928 and went out to Chicago to play piano in Sammy Stewart's orchestra," which we talked about on our first tape, "Including some dates in Columbus, Ohio. but that fall Horace left Stewart and decided to form a new

band of his own. He sent to Indianapolis for Raymond Syd Valentine (trumpet, and leader of the Patent Leather Kids of Gennett record fame) and Cleve Bottoms on alto sax. Duncan Schiedt dates this as late 1928, when the band was in Columbus, Ohio. The new personnel was given as: Syd Valentine, Red Harland, Sprat Morton, playing trumpets." And then here it says, "Unknown trombones." Do you know who the trombones were at that time? You're in Columbus, Ohio, 1928, Syd Valentine.
Yes. I had a trombonist named Nathaniel Atkins, and Ed Fant --
Okay, but how do you spell that, F---
-- a-n-t. Ed Fant. I also had a great saxophonist, but of this who eventually became great that wasn't named in that (inaudible). I don't know why.
The alto saxes it states here as Cleve Bottoms and Van Sherrill.
Van Sherrill is out of Toledo, Ohio. He's a mortician now, and he was a great good saxophonist. But that isn't the one I'm speaking of.
Well, and it --
What about the tenor sax? Who is that?
Tenor sax they have listed as Cleo Good, Dad Good.
There is a Cleo Good. There was a Cleo Good who was a tenor saxophonist, but I had two. I know why they didn't, ... don't remember whether
Yeah, they list only one. Who was the other?

A guy named Joe Thomas was the great tenor saxophonist, with Jimmie Lunceford was the great (inaudible) band. I brought him out of Columbus, Ohio. And he had an alto. I immediately put him (inaudible) on tenor, because he had such a drive. what he did for the Lunceford band. Of course, you know the particular bunch of (inaudible).
Right.
He is also a mortician, in Atlantic Kansas City
Is that right?

Yes. But he comes out of retirement, speaking of that particular thing, every now and then and he makes appearances on TV, on the -- sometimes the big shows that migrate out of LA might (inaudible) out of Ellic and all. And he ma still plays.
Huh. Let's see, Also they weren't able to list the drummer here. They have Luke Look Stewart, guitar, Sylvester Turpin on bass, and do you recall who the drummer was at that time?
I had a drummer named Jimmy King. He's deceased now. And when you said Look Stewart, the Luke banjo player -- played banjo.
I see. Okay, good. He did not play guitar? He was playing banjo?
No, he played banjo. But I got another guy in there in the band should have been in there, a trumpet player, Jonah Jones.
At that time?
Yes, because we -- this is the band who went to Buffalo, New York. Luke Stewart is still in Buffalo. He never left.
(Laughter)
But the guy who didn't get the correct in there (inaudible) the personnel overlooked.
